description:
Tighten parent guidance so nonblocking orchestration does not invite the parent to concurrently edit delegated scope, while preserving Beadwork's parent-owned ticket and goal lifecycle.

## Background

Core minions guidance says `orchestrate` is background work that should not block the parent, but does not define what work the parent may safely continue. Beadwork run mode tells the parent to orchestrate but does not state strongly enough that it is a manager-only loop. Dogfood feedback showed parent-induced semantic churn when the parent and children independently modified the same problem. Models can also choose to execute a decomposed epic without a human typing `/bw run`; after the goal-entry issue lands, guidance must tell them to use the explicit transition rather than approximating run mode through lower-level ticket calls.

## Required guidance

### General minions: cooperative sidecar

- Use sidecar orchestration only for slices independent of the parent's continuing work.
- Once scope is delegated, the parent must not edit that delegated scope while the child is live; message or halt the child instead.
- The parent may continue user interaction, inspection, planning, or non-overlapping work.
- Path intent and overlap notices remain advisory, not locks.
- A parent turn ending while children run is normal, but the parent must not represent delegated work as complete.

### Agent-initiated Beadwork goal entry

- When the parent model deliberately chooses to execute an existing, already-decomposed open epic, call `beadwork_start_goal({ epic_id })` instead of merely imitating `/bw run` with `ready`, ticket mutations, and `orchestrate`.
- Starting a goal is an explicit manager-intent transition. It arms persistent policy and queues continuation; it does not implement, dispatch, or complete the epic in the tool call.
- Do not auto-start goal mode merely because an epic exists, becomes ready, or was just created. Planning/decomposition and executing the graph remain distinct decisions.
- Human `/bw run <epic-id>` and model `beadwork_start_goal` are equivalent entry surfaces for the same lifecycle.

### Beadwork goal mode: manager-only

- Parent refreshes ready/show, starts issues, composes complete tasks, dispatches, adjudicates handoffs, launches required independent reviews, dispatches fixes, and keeps ready work in flight.
- Parent does not implement a delegated ticket concurrently with its live child.
- Children do not start/close/reopen tickets or start goals; parent-owned mutation boundary remains.
- Implementation child tasks must explicitly require an atomic ticket-scoped commit and returned commit SHA. Follow repository instructions to stage only owned files; no broad staging.
- Reviewer children start only after the implementer settles and inspect the named SHA/ticket with `git show`, not the whole dirty checkout.
- Settlement remains evidence, not acceptance or ticket closure.

## Scope / ownership

- minions tool promptGuidelines, `skill.ts`, README and concise learning copy
- Beadwork `prompt.ts` standing run appendix, agent goal-start discovery guidance, `/bw run`/`beadwork_start_goal` injected prompt copy if required, and prompt/golden tests
- terminology must use canonical `agent`, not the removed `role` selector

## Explicit non-goals

- Do not add a group operating-mode field in this epic.
- Do not infer behavior from opaque `domain.source`.
- Do not import minions runtime/AgentTree into Beadwork.
- Do not add locks, edit interception, commit detection, worktrees, polling, or a child result schema.
- Do not make children mutate Beadwork tickets or enter parent goal mode.
- Do not create `run_epic`/`implement_epic` aliases or implicit goal selection.

## Acceptance behavior

- A parent given generic orchestrate guidance can distinguish safe non-overlapping sidecar work from unsafe concurrent editing.
- A model that decides to execute a polished epic discovers and uses `beadwork_start_goal`, while a planning-only model does not enter run mode automatically.
- Goal-mode prompt clearly establishes manager-only behavior and the implementation→commit SHA→independent review chain regardless of whether entry came from `/bw run` or the tool.
- Prompt tests lock the negative constraints without freezing incidental prose.
- Existing ticket/scope/none review-policy branches and taskType next questions remain correct.

## Tests and validation

Update focused minions skill/prompt tests and Beadwork prompt/in-process orchestration assertions. Cover both human-command and agent-tool goal entry, explicit-vs-automatic initiation, and identical manager-only policy. Avoid giant incidental snapshots; assert the operative boundaries and closed doors. Run scoped lint/test/typecheck for both packages. Commit atomically with this issue id.
title: Define sidecar and Beadwork manager-only orchestration boundaries
